source.title: The Neutral Mask: How Alignment Training Provides Shallow Alignment while Leaving Partisan Structure Intact in a Large Language Model

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses safety-alignment results as motivation and analogy, but its own experiments concern partisan political orientation, not the safety behaviours named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on safety fine-tuning and shallow alignment, but reports no new harmful-request compliance, refusal, aligned-versus-base per-token KL, compliant-prefix, suffix, decoding, or safety-training results. Its own partisan-orientation results are recorded as findings about a related but different construct; cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares Llama 3.1 8B base and Instruct on partisan political orientation (probe projections, SAE features, feature steering). It reports no harmful-request compliance, refusal rates, per-token KL on harmful prompts, prefill/suffix/decoding attacks, safety fine-tuning, or deepening training. Safety-alignment work (Qi et al.) is cited only as motivation and analogy. Its findings concern a related but different construct and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The authors conclude that alignment training leaves partisan geometry intact but severs its causal path to generation. This makes the neutrality functional and potentially fragile. They suggest the pattern parallels safety and toxicity findings and may generalize, while noting the study covers one model (Llama 3.1 8B).
record.recipe_differences: The study compares the Llama 3.1 8B base and Instruct checkpoints using political prompts, a partisan probe, an SAE, and feature-level steering. It does not apply the harmful- or benign-example safety fine-tuning recipe in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed political output depends on whether the model is base or Instruct and on whether policy-feature directions are steered; the paper also reports that the non-political steak prompt behaves similarly across the two models.

fits_no_version.finding: Instruct-model partisan scores along an Instruct-derived probe are compressed versus base: range −0.011 to 0.388 (σ=0.07) vs −0.5 to 1.253 (σ=0.235).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Llama 3.1 8B, alignment post-training compresses and centers projections along a partisan probe direction on open-ended political prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: The Instruct model gives neutral, multi-perspective completions on all 84 prompts; the base model often adopts a partisan voice.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment post-training yields consistently balanced output on open-ended political stems.

fits_no_version.finding: Five manually identified policy SAE features are zero on all 84 Instruct prompts but fire sporadically in base. Unique active features drop 706→244. Only 28.3% of active features overlap per prompt.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment post-training silences policy-encoding SAE features and narrows feature usage, while the dictionary directions remain.

fits_no_version.finding: At α=6, steering on policy-feature decoder directions shifts base-model political text toward the steered stance. The Instruct model's text stays balanced although the probe score shifts identically.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Alignment post-training disconnects partisan representational directions from generation rather than removing them (a 'disconnect-not-delete' pattern analogous to shallow alignment).

record.problems: The analysis is limited to one model family and 84 prompts. The partisan probe direction was trained on the Instruct model; the authors say interpreting base-model scores as partisan valence would require a base-specific probe. Identification of political features relies on manual inspection. Steering-output effects are described qualitatively, without reported uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 reports additional score shifts for multiple steering directions and strengths, but these are geometric projections along the partisan axis rather than safety-behaviour outcomes; they are not included as separate rows for this claim.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning; no harmful-request compliance measured.
No benign fine-tuning; no harmful-request compliance measured.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks on refusal. The activation steering targets partisan output, not safety refusal.
SAE features studied are partisan or policy features, not safety-carrying weights or ranks.
Safety data and training objective are not examined as causes of shallowness.
No safety-deepening training is applied or evaluated.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/discusses classification is right, and the rows are correctly unlinked (versions none). Score shifts in Table 2 are geometric, identical by construction across models, and rightly excluded. The paper's parallel to shallow safety alignment is an analogy drawn from cited work, not a tested safety result. No embedded instructions were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful fine-tuning or harmful-request compliance/refusal evaluation.
No benign fine-tuning or harmful-request compliance/refusal evaluation.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement on harmful prompts.
No compliant-prefix, suffix, or decoding intervention testing safety behaviour.
Feature analysis and steering concern partisan political content, not safety behaviour.
No safety-training data or objective is examined as a cause of shallow safety.
No training intended to deepen safety or evaluation of its robustness.

rows.subject: Llama 3.1 8B
rows.stage_stated: base; pre-trained, not trained to follow instructions or aligned with behavioral norms
rows.operation_detail: Projected hidden states for 84 prompts onto the Instruct-derived Layer 18 partisan probe direction.

conditions.value: 84 prompts spanning political, historical, scientific, and non-obviously political topics

rows.measure: Range, mean, and standard deviation of partisan scores along the shared probe direction
rows.note: The authors caution that this shared Instruct-trained direction does not establish partisan valence in the base model without a base-specific probe.

rows.subject: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
rows.stage_stated: Instruct; post-trained with supervised finetuning, rejection sampling, and DPO
rows.operation_detail: Projected hidden states for 84 prompts onto the Layer 18 partisan probe direction.

conditions.value: 84 prompts spanning political, historical, scientific, and non-obviously political topics

rows.measure: Range, mean, and standard deviation of partisan scores along the probe direction
rows.baseline: Base model: range 1.753, from −0.5 to 1.253; µ = 0.101, σ = 0.235
rows.note: The authors describe the Instruct scores as compressed and centered relative to the base model.

rows.subject: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Generated responses to the 84 prompts and assessed their described political framing.

conditions.value: Base model responses to identical prompts

rows.measure: Whether responses adopt a partisan voice or present balanced, multi-perspective output
rows.baseline: Base model outputs vary across prompts and sometimes adopt a partisan voice
rows.value: The Instruct model generated neutral, multi-perspective output across all 84 prompts, according to the authors.
rows.note: This is a qualitative political-orientation result, not a safety refusal or harmful-compliance measure.

rows.subject: Llama 3.1 8B
rows.operation_detail: Checked activation of selected SAE features on the 84 prompts.
rows.measure: Prompt-level occurrence of activation for identified policy-related features
rows.value: Feature 9036 activated on the Heritage Foundation prompt; Feature 12677 activated on six prompts, including political and non-political prompts.
rows.note: The paper does not state activation counts for the other three selected features in the base model.

rows.subject: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Checked activation of the five identified SAE policy features on the 84 prompts.
rows.measure: Activation of identified policy-related SAE features
rows.baseline: Base model: Features 9036 and 12677 activated on the prompts described by the authors.
rows.value: All five policy features were zero on all 84 prompts.
rows.note: The authors say the features were zero, not merely attenuated.

rows.subject: Llama 3.1 8B
rows.operation_detail: Counted unique SAE features active across 84 prompts.
rows.note: The paper gives the Instruct comparison as 244 unique features, a 65% reduction.

rows.subject: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Counted unique SAE features active across 84 prompts.
rows.value: 244 unique features; the paper describes this as a 65% reduction compared with the base model.
rows.note: The authors also report that only 1 of the 20 highest-ranked features by |βi| was active at all in the Instruct model.

rows.subject: Llama 3.1 8B
rows.operation_detail: Added scaled SAE decoder directions to Layer 18 hidden states during generation.

conditions.value: 12 prompts spanning political, scientific, and non-political topics

rows.measure: Qualitative effect on generated political content
rows.value: On politically resonant prompts, steering produced text matching the feature direction; examples include dismissive anti-Biden rhetoric for Feature 9036 and progressive advocacy for Feature 19268.
rows.note: The paper reports 360 output generations per model across the full steering experiment; this row records the described political-content effect, not a safety outcome.

rows.subject: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Added scaled SAE decoder directions to Layer 18 hidden states during generation.

conditions.value: 12 prompts spanning political, scientific, and non-political topics

rows.measure: Qualitative effect on generated political content
rows.value: The model continued to produce balanced text under the policy-feature perturbations; the authors describe a subtle framing shift but say the output remained informative and non-partisan.
rows.note: The authors report the same general pattern across prompts; this is partisan-generation resistance, not safety-guardrail resistance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
